No final-status guard exists -- only update_application_status_for_documents (used elsewhere) checks FINAL_STATUSES, but request_document bypasses that function entirely.

extra.message: DoS: Export endpoints load all records unbounded into memory

metadata.proof: SOURCE: Authenticated admin triggers GET /api/admin/exports/applications (line 1503), /api/admin/exports/decisions (line 1534), or /api/admin/exports/documents (line 1565). SINK: All three export endpoints call .all() with no LIMIT clause (applications at line 1511, decisions at line 1536, documents at line 1569), loading every matching row into a Python list before serializing to CSV/JSON. An attacker with admin access -- or who has compromised an admin session -- can trigger these endpoints to consume unbounded server memory proportional to the total row count of the applications/decisions/documents tables, causing memory exhaustion. No pagination, streaming, or row cap is applied.

extra.message: DoS: document_review_queue loads all matching documents unbounded into memory

metadata.proof: SOURCE: Authenticated support_specialist, underwriter, or admin sends GET /api/documents/review-queue (line 1119). SINK: Line 1131 calls db.scalars(stmt).all() with no LIMIT clause. For support_specialist and admin roles, the query has no scope filter beyond an optional status_filter -- it loads every KYCDocument row in the system into memory. Combined with eager-loaded relationships (application, borrower_profile, document_type, reviewer), this can exhaust server memory when the document table is large. No pagination, row cap, or streaming is applied.
